extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (researchers in computational algebra / algebraic geometry who use SINGULAR libraries such as sheafcoh.lib, JMBTest.lib, JMSConst.lib, alexpoly.lib)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation and usage specifications for SINGULAR library procedures (sheaf cohomology, J-marked basis tests, J-marked scheme construction, plane curve singularity invariants). Contains usage signatures, assumptions, return types, notes and examples for each procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: CM regularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: CM_regularity(M); M module. Assume: M is graded, and it comes assigned with an admissible degree vector as an attribute. Return: integer, the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of coker(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: procedure calls mres. Example provided: assign isHomog attribute, call CM_regularity(M) -> returns an integer (example: 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: sheafCohBGG
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sheafCohBGG(M,l,h); M module, l,h int. Assume: M is graded with an admissible degree vector attribute, h >= l, and the basering has n+1 variables. Return: intmat, cohomology of twists of the coherent sheaf F on P^n associated to coker(M) over the range d = l..h.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: table diagram with rows h^n(F(d))..h^0(F(d)) and chi(F(d)). A '-' denotes zero, '*' denotes a negative entry (= dimension not yet determined), and an uncomputed entry is shown differently. Based on BGG correspondence and Tate resolution. Note: sheafCohBGG does not compute all values; to determine all values use sheafCohBGG(M,l-n,h+n). Examples and full example outputs are given. Experimental/computational timing notes included.

rubrics_metrics.name: sheafCohBGG2
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sheafCohBGG2(M,l,h); M module, l,h int. Assume: M is graded with admissible degree vector attribute, h >= l, basering has n+1 variables. Return: intmat cohomology of twists of the coherent sheaf F on P^n for d = l..h.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: same intmat diagram as sheafCohBGG. Additional behavior: if printlevel >= 1, step-by-step timings printed; printlevel >= 2 adds progress debug messages; >=3 prints intermediate results. Based on BGG and Tate resolution. Experimental version intended to require less memory. Examples show comparative timings versus other methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: sheafCoh
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sheafCoh(M,l,h); M module, l,h int. Assume: M is graded and has an admissible degree vector attribute, h >= l, base ring S has n+1 variables. Return: intmat, cohomology of twists of the coherent sheaf F on P^n associated to coker(M) over d = l..h.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: same diagram (h^n..h^0 and chi). A '-' denotes zero. Procedure is based on local duality. By default uses mres to compute Ext modules; can be called with additional parameter 'sres' to use sres instead. Examples and timings provided (and references).

rubrics_metrics.name: dimH
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dimH(i,M,d); M module, i,d int. Assume: M is graded and has an admissible degree vector attribute. Return: int, the vector space dimension of H^i(F(d)) for F the coherent sheaf on P^n associated to coker(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: procedure is based on local duality. Examples show calls like dimH(0,M,2) -> integer outputs for several i,d combinations. See also sheafCoh and sheafCohBGG references.

rubrics_metrics.name: dimGradedPart
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dimGradedPart(M,d); M module, d int. Assume: M is graded and has an admissible degree vector attribute. Return: int, the vector space dimension of the graded part of degree d of coker(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Example shows use on maxideal modules and after shifting grading via attrib(M,'isHomog',intvec(...)). Typical outputs: dimGradedPart(M,k) -> integer. Useful for computing dimensions of graded pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: displayCohom
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: displayCohom(data,l,h,n); data intmat, l,h,n int. Assume: h >= l, data is return value of sheafCoh or sheafCohBGG, and basering has n+1 variables. Return: none (display only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: prints the intmat in the sheaf cohomology diagram (h^n..h^0 and chi). A '-' denotes zero entry, '*' denotes a negative entry (= dimension not yet determined). Use to format and visualize results from sheafCoh/sheafCohBGG.

rubrics_metrics.name: J-marked basis test (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview (JMBTest.lib): perform the J-marked basis test via the criterion using Eliahou-Kervaire (EK) polynomials. All polynomials must be homogeneous and arranged by degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental steps: construct the Vm polynomials via VConstructor; construct EK polynomials as in [BCLR]; reduce EK polynomials using the Vm's; if any EK polynomial reduces to a nonzero remainder modulo Vm, the given set is not a J-marked basis. Algorithm terminates only if ordering is rp; number of reduction steps is bounded. References: [CR], [BCLR].

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimus
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Minimus(L); L ideal generated by variables. Return: list V containing the minimal variable generating the ideal L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Input must be an ideal generated by variables. Example: ideal I=y,x,z; Minimus(I) -> x. Intended as a utility to extract the minimal variable generator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximus
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Maximus(L); L ideal generated by variables. Return: list V containing the maximal variable generating the ideal L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Input must be an ideal generated by variables. Example: ideal I=y,x,z; Maximus(I) -> z. Utility complementary to Minimus.

rubrics_metrics.name: StartOrderingV
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: StartOrdina(V,G); V list, G list. Return: list R (ordered polynomials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Input Vm, G. This procedure uses OrderingV to get ordered polynomials as in [BCLR]. Example shows how jmps are arranged and StartOrderingV returns structured lists grouped by degree/order. Helps prepare data for the J-marked test.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestJMark
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: TestJMark(G); G list (list of J-marked polynomials arranged by degree). Return: int: boolean evaluation (True=1 / False=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure performs the J-marked basis test as described in JMBTest.lib. The input is a list of jmp arranged by degree (G1 is a list of lists). Output prints status (e.g., 'NOT A BASIS') and returns 0/1. Example provided demonstrating a NOT A BASIS result.

rubrics_metrics.name: JMSConst library overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview (JMSConst.lib): constructs J-Marked Schemes by constructing V polynomials and reducing EK polynomials w.r.t. them, collecting resulting coefficients. Algorithm terminates only if ordering is rp; reduction steps bounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References same as JMBTest.lib. Provides higher-level construction routines for J-marked schemes, building on the J-marked test methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: BorelCheck
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: BorelCheck(Borid,r); Borid ideal (monomial ideal), r ring. Return: int d. Purpose: checks whether the Borel moves produce elements belonging to Borid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Input must be a monomial ideal. Example: BorelCheck(y^2*z,y*z^2,z^3,y^5, r) -> 1 (true). Use to verify Borel-closedness of monomial ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: JMarkedScheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: JMarkedScheme(Borid, r); Borid ideal, r ring. Return: list: Jms. Purpose: automatically performs the whole construction of the J-marked scheme for the given monomial ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Example call returns a list of polynomial relations (expressed in c(...) notation) forming the J-marked scheme equations. Use when needing the explicit scheme equations from a Borel-stable monomial ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: resolutiongraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: resolutiongraph(INPUT); INPUT poly or list. INPUT must be either a REDUCED bivariate polynomial defining a plane curve singularity, or the output of hnexpansion(f,'ess'), or related derived forms such as develop(f) or a list containing contact matrix and characteristic exponents. Return: intmat, the incidence matrix of the resolution graph (diagonal entries are vertex weights; negative diagonal entries correspond to strict transforms of branches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: If unsure whether INPUT is reduced, use squarefree(INPUT) first. If Hamburger-Noether expansion will be reused, compute hnexpansion first and pass its output. Example demonstrates multi-line integer matrix output representing the resolution graph.

rubrics_metrics.name: totalmultiplicities
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: totalmultiplicities(INPUT); INPUT poly or list (same allowed inputs as resolutiongraph). Return: list L of three integer matrices: L[1] incidence matrix of resolution graph; L[2] matrix with total multiplicities (rows=vertices, columns=branches); L[3] matrix with strict multiplicities (same indexing as L[2]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: The total multiplicity of a branch along an exceptional divisor is multiplicity of that divisor in the total transform of the branch. Advice: use hnexpansion output if required for other purposes. Example shows the three matrices produced for a sample combined polynomial input.

rubrics_metrics.name: alexanderpolynomial (intro)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: alexanderpolynomial(INPUT); INPUT poly or list. INPUT same accepted forms as resolutiongraph/totalmultiplicities (reduced bivariate polynomial or hnexpansion output, etc.). Return: (creates) the Alexander polynomial of the plane curve singularity / related invariants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: The library computes resolution graph, total multiplicities, Alexander polynomial and zeta function of monodromy. See references and related procedures (hnexpansion, develop, extdevelop) for preparing INPUT. Examples and cross-references appear in nearby sections.
